newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil coffee consumers pay for rise in bean price.
newsitem.headline: Brazil coffee consumers pay for rise in bean price.

text.p: Brazilian roasters have already started to raise the price of coffee in the shops because of higher green bean prices and consumers should expect further increases, said David Nahum, secretary-general of the Brazilian Coffee Industry Association (Abic).

"We are already starting to reflect the rising price in raw material in retail prices," Nahum said ahead of the first formal meeting of Brazil's new coffee council held this afternoon in Vitoria, Espirito Santo state.
"Some companies have raised their prices by 30 to 50 percent but raw material prices have risen 100 percent. And retail prices will eventually see a 100 percent rise," he added.
A kilo of coffee in Brazilian shops now costs around 5.60 to 5.80 reais as opposed to four to 4.20 reais at the beginning of January, Nahum said.
The higher retail prices had already started to have an impact on domestic consumption, he said.
"We normally see a 10 percent fall in consumption during the Brazilian summer. But we are also seeing some impact because of the higher prices which is too early to quantify," Nahum said.
-- Caroline Bulloch, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 5074151
